newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong blames flood on two tree trunks.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong blames flood on two tree trunks.

text.p: Floods which inundated more than 1,000 Hong Kong homes, swamped farmland and wrecked fish ponds, were blamed on two large tree trunks on Thursday.
Torrential rain pelted the territory this week, causing floods and landslips in the rural New Territories as the wettest summer here in over a century showed no let-up.
Two three-metre logs blocked the entrance to a crucial dain, and caused water levels to rise, while fish escaped from overflowing ponds, local media reported.
"The ginger, the yams and the leafy vegetables have all been destroyed," said 78-year-old Lo Tai as she scooped water from her flooded village home.
The rainy season, which runs from July to September, has been the worst since weather records began here in 1884.
